subject: RLA
title: Identifying an Author's Argument
standardTag: RLA.R.2 — Determine central ideas and themes
tipLine: Take your time — you don't need to catch everything on the first read.

vocabTerms.definition: a statement someone argues is true
facts, examples, or data that back up a claim

blocks.heading: What's a claim vs. evidence?
blocks.body: A claim is what the author wants you to believe. Evidence backs it up — facts, examples, or data. Strong readers learn to spot the difference: the claim is the point being argued, and the evidence is what's offered to convince you it's true.

blocks.question: "City council should fund the new bike lanes — three neighboring cities saw a 40% drop in traffic accidents after similar projects." What is the claim?
options: City council should fund the bike lanes
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — that's the position being argued. The accident stat is the evidence.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite — the claim is the position being argued: that city council should fund the bike lanes. The accident statistic is the evidence used to support it.
